elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: The Section 5(a) parenthetical floor ("but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services") is deleted and replaced with an express statement: "and Client will have no minimum purchase or volume commitment." No other take-or-pay, shortfall, or volume-cap mechanic survives in the cited text (the Section 6 carve-outs referencing the minimums are conformed away).

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained operative language: "Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits 'A' and 'B'" and, for other services, fees "will vary depending on the services utilized"; invoices are issued monthly for "the requested Hosting Services and Support Services and any other agreed-upon services." Payment is thus tied to requested/ordered services only.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: its stated condition (an existing minimum commitment) no longer applies because the redline deletes the monthly fee floor entirely, so there is no commitment to term-limit. The stronger preferred outcome subsumes this fallback constraint.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with the minimum monthly fees removed from Section 5(a), there is no residual commitment for Client to reduce; no reduction-notice mechanic is required to reach the same or better outcome.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no shortfall can arise because no minimum volume or fee floor remains, and no penalty, shortfall charge, or contingent payment formula is retained in Section 5(a) or Section 6.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the take-or-pay floor is struck from Section 5(a) and replaced with an express no-minimum statement, while the retained sentence continues to tie fees to "requested" Hosting and Support Services and to services "utilized."

Fallback elements are conditional on a surviving commitment; because the commitment is deleted outright, the 12-month limit, 30-day reduction right, and true-up mechanic have no subject matter and are satisfied without needing operative text.

Minimality holds: two surgical edits only. The Section 6 deletions of "(other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4)" are conforming, not cosmetic — retaining them would leave a carve-out pointing at a deleted (and already mis-cross-referenced) fee floor. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or extraneous requirements were added.

Intent is preserved: monthly invoicing, the 15-day payment term, the negotiated-fee mechanic for other services, the one-year price-increase freeze, and the most-favoured-rate covenant for Hosting Services all survive without contradiction, and the removal leaves no dangling defined term or cross-reference.

Scoping is correct: Section 3(i) (credit report per borrower submitted through the Interface) is usage-triggered and Section 3 storage/bandwidth figures are service specifications, so neither was redlined as a Customer commitment.

Drafting note only (not a defect): the added phrase "and Client will have no minimum purchase or volume commitment" is affirmative belt-and-braces; deletion of the parenthetical alone would likely suffice, but the express statement is concise and directly tracks the checklist element.
